## Runs 6–7 — both-side SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check`)

Raw Rxx is formed from sr1_X divided by the measured drain current (sr0_X/−1e6), then plotted before the FFT. Run 6 at n = +3.2×10¹² cm⁻², D = 0 covers 0–10 T in 10 mT steps above 1 T; run 7 at n = −1.2×10¹², D = 0 covers 10→0.3 T in 20 mT steps. Both completed without clipping (Rxx maxima ≈ 530/587 Ω against 5 kΩ full scale), with stable ~10 nA drain current; the Keithley-current excursions are isolated read noise around pA to ~100 pA levels, below the 1 nA trip. The FFT windows below are an exploratory side comparison, not a stacking verdict; the calibrated lever-arm **ratio** comes from run 5, while F_L still inherits its geometry-prior scale.

# Runs 6 and 7, raw data before FFT. Channel arithmetic follows device card.
from hera.analysis import sdh_fft, sdh_onset
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 7), constrained_layout=True)
for j, (rid, density, cutoff) in enumerate([(6, 3.2, 1.3), (7, -1.2, 0.7)]):
    rr = run(rid)
    B = rr.col('magnet_field')
    I = rr.col('sr0_X') / -1e6
    R = rr.col('sr1_X') / I
    order = np.argsort(B)
    B, R = B[order], R[order]
    axs[0,j].plot(B, R, lw=0.8)
    axs[0,j].set(title=f'Run {rid}, n={density:+.1f}e12, D=0: raw Rxx', xlabel='B (T)', ylabel='Rxx (ohm)')
    f, power = sdh_fft(R[:,None], B, b_range=(cutoff, 10), nfft=4096, bg_degree=5, log=False)
    y = power[0]
    axs[1,j].plot(f, y, lw=0.9)
    axs[1,j].axvline(10.339*abs(density), color='k', ls=':', lw=1, label='F_L geometry prior')
    axs[1,j].set(xlim=(0, 45), xlabel='frequency (T)', ylabel='FFT power', title=f'FFT: {cutoff:.1f}–10 T; B-space polynomial background')
    axs[1,j].legend(fontsize=8)
    peaks,_ = find_peaks(y)
    peaks = sorted((i for i in peaks if 3<f[i]<40), key=lambda i:y[i], reverse=True)[:6]
    print(f'run {rid}: strongest FFT peaks {[round(float(f[i]),1) for i in peaks]} T; F_L={10.339*abs(density):.1f} T')
    on = sdh_onset(R,B,b_lo=0.3,b_hi=10,r_full_scale=5000)
    print(on.summary())
plt.show()

**Read and next step:** The electron record has a robust ≈7 T component and higher components near ≈22 and ≈29 T (run 6); the 29 T line may be a sum/breakdown tone, so neither its amplitude nor a one-density match decides stacking. `sdh_onset` marks the 7 T line censored at the low edge and flags harmonic relations; its low-field onset is therefore an unresolved bound, while the higher-frequency content first clears its threshold around 1.3–1.9 T. The hole record has lower-frequency structure but sits in the investigation's near-CNP, close-tone exception regime and cannot offer the same density leverage. Choose the electron side for a D = 0 fan spanning n = +2.7…+3.2×10¹² and B = 1…10 T, with a 1/B Nyquist and five-period check on the model's light branch; the fan will test F(n), a shared Luttinger scale, and whether the 29 T component tracks a sum or a separate pocket. Region B's parallel CNP ridge (run 5) can add ~0.43×10¹² to local density and remains an explicit mosaic confound.

## HERA — electron-side D = 0 Landau fan for the tetralayer FS count (`landau-fan-vti`)

> **05:24** · FS-count electron fan: D=0, n +3.2 to +2.7e12 cm^-2 (12), B +1 to +10 T (901 x 10 mT), sr1 50 uV, 2.4 s dwell · **ETA ~16:24** (≈11h)

Runs 6–7 (ana cells 14–16) favor the electron side: run 6 at n = +3.2×10¹² has ≈7, 22 and 29 T content, while the hole spot is restricted to the near-CNP exception regime. This fan asks whether those components follow two branches, a branch plus harmonic/sum orbit, or one Luttinger-frequency pocket across density; the ≈29 T line is not assigned in advance. The run-5 CNP calibration fixes D = 0 and the gate ratio, but its absolute n scale remains a geometry prior; region B's parallel ridge may add a second local density.

**Grid and cost:** n = +3.2→+2.7×10¹² cm⁻² in 12 paired-gate points, B = 1→10 T in 901 uniform-B rows (10 mT), with 2.4 s fast dwell (8τ at the recorded 0.3 s, 24 dB/oct), fixed sr1 50 µV sensitivity, and 10 nA nominal bias. At n_max, F_L = 33.1 T and the worst Δ(1/B) = 0.0099 T⁻¹ gives ≈3 samples/period; the 0.0455×10¹² density step gives 2.1 samples per ray period at 1 T. The ABAB model's light branch at n_min is ≈5.7 T, giving ≈5.1 periods over 1–10 T (δF = 1.11 T). Starting from the handoff's 0 T costs ≈7 min of bare positioning; the 9 T recorded traverse is ≥66 min, 10,812 grid points × (2.4 s dwell + ~0.25 s read) ≈8.0 h, 901 driver settles × 3 s ≈45 min, plus row/reset overhead; run 6's actual 2.0 h for 921 field points supports **≈11 h** with margin. The global worst R corner is the low-n/high-B end; run 6 peaked at 530 Ω, so 5 kΩ full scale provides headroom with usable resolution. Coverage is deliberately the high-density electron window; including the entire D = 0 gate line to the hole limit would require roughly eight times as many density points at the 1 T ray-Nyquist floor and would cross the high-MR CNP.

**Preflight and checkpoints:** The cell checks live thermometry, base T, the handoff's near-zero field and gates, Si = 0, heater/output state, bias and lock-in τ/slope, and validator acceptance before moving. Watch the first three landed B rows for flat/railed channels, leakage and wrong gate coordinates; review at approximately 3, 6 and 9 T for sustained leakage, field/temperature drift, clipping, and emerging fan structure. A sustained >1 nA Keithley gate current on two consecutive grid points requests a sweep stop. After the sweep, read the native TSV before FFT, overlay both ABAB and ABCA forward-model F(n), pin one global density scale, screen harmonics and the 29 T sum-tone possibility, and retain region-B mosaic and adjacent-layer-number alternatives if the trajectories demand them. Leave the field at 10 T for the next science decision and return the gates to 0 V after the sweep.

# Electron-side D=0 FS-count fan; run-5 calibration, runs 6/7 spot-check design.
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

CAL = dict(c_tg=0.0027960593093052633, c_bg=0.002160696465377614,
           n_offset=-0.08937933224099137, D_offset=-0.013)
ns = np.linspace(3.2, 2.7, 12)  # 1e12 cm^-2; high-density electron window
Ds = np.zeros_like(ns)           # V/nm
Vtgs, Vbgs = calc_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])
B_vec = np.round(np.linspace(1.0, 10.0, 901), 4)  # 10 mT, monotonic upward
assert len(ns) == 12 and len(B_vec) == 901 and np.all(np.diff(B_vec) > 0)
assert B_vec[-1] <= B_SESSION_CAP == 10.0
assert TG_MIN == -0.3 and TG_MAX == 1.0 and BG_MIN == -1.3 and BG_MAX == 2.0
for vtg, vbg in zip(Vtgs, Vbgs):
    k_tg.volt.validate(float(vtg)); k_bg.volt.validate(float(vbg))
magnet.field.validate(float(B_vec[0])); magnet.field.validate(float(B_vec[-1]))
print(f'plan: n {ns[0]:+.3f} to {ns[-1]:+.3f}e12, D=0; '
      f'TG {Vtgs.min():+.4f}..{Vtgs.max():+.4f} V, BG {Vbgs.min():+.4f}..{Vbgs.max():+.4f} V; '
      f'B {B_vec[0]:.2f}..{B_vec[-1]:.2f} T ({len(B_vec)} rows x {len(ns)} points)')
print('roundtrip endpoints:', calc_nD(Vtgs[0], Vbgs[0], **CAL),
      calc_nD(Vtgs[-1], Vbgs[-1], **CAL))

# Silent preconditions: read actual state before positioning or gate writes.
assert_thermometry_live('T_sample', VTI.temp_logfile_candidates['T_sample'], max_age=15, max_period=12)
assert_thermometry_live('T_vaporizer', VTI.temp_logfile_candidates['T_vaporizer'], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T, _Tv, _B = T_sample(), T_vaporizer(), magnet.field()
_tg, _bg, _si = k_tg.volt(), k_bg.volt(), k_si()
_ps, _out = magnet.persistent_switch_on(), magnet.output_enabled()
_hr = (heater.sample_range(), heater.vaporizer_range())
_amp, _tau, _slope = sr1.amplitude(), sr1.time_constant(), sr1.filter_slope()
print(f'precondition: T_sample={_T:.3f} K (1.0..1.5), T_vaporizer={_Tv:.3f} K (<1.5), '
      f'B={_B:+.4f} T (~0), TG={_tg:+.4f} V (0), BG={_bg:+.4f} V (0), Si={_si:+.4f} V (0)')
print(f'precondition: PS heater={_ps} (True), output={_out} (True), heater ranges={_hr} ((0,0)), '
      f'drive={_amp:.3f} V (1), sr1 tau={_tau:.3f} s (0.3), slope={_slope} dB/oct (24)')
assert 1.0 <= _T <= 1.5 and _Tv < 1.5 and abs(_B) < 0.05
assert abs(_tg) < 0.01 and abs(_bg) < 0.01 and abs(_si) < 0.01
assert _ps and _out and _hr == (0, 0)
assert abs(_amp - 1.0) < 0.02 and abs(_tau - 0.3) < 1e-6 and _slope == 24
assert dc205.voltage_range() == 2 and dc205.output() == 1

# Set a fixed sensitivity; sr0's 20 mV range and 0.3 s filter are inherited from state0.
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f'sr1 sensitivity={sr1.sensitivity():.2e} V (expect 50 uV), '
      f'sr0 sensitivity={sr0.sensitivity():.3g} V (expect 20 mV)')
assert abs(sr1.sensitivity() - 50e-6) < 1e-9 and abs(sr0.sensitivity() - 0.02) < 1e-6

# Blocking VTI ramp: measured readback after positioning, before the data run starts.
magnet.field(float(B_vec[0]))
_Bstart = magnet.field()
print(f'positioned B={_Bstart:+.4f} T; expected {B_vec[0]:+.4f} T')
assert abs(_Bstart - B_vec[0]) < 0.02

mc = dict(meas_config)
mc['Si (V)'] = _si
mc['sample_temperature:'] = _T
mc['comments'] = ('landau-fan-vti electron FS count; n +3.2 to +2.7e12 cm^-2, D=0, '
                  'B 1 to 10 T x 10 mT, 12 paired-gate points, sr1 50 uV, fast_delay 2.4 s; cal run 5')
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')
s.add_comment('electron region B_1-B_2; D=0 V/nm; n +3.2 to +2.7e12 cm^-2 (12); '
              'B +1 to +10 T (901 x 10 mT); TG +0.9836 to +0.8403 V, BG +1.1663 to +0.9809 V; '
              'Si=0 V; run-5 calibration; sr1 50 uV, tau 0.3 s/24 dB, fast_delay 2.4 s')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, float(Vbgs[0]))
s.ramp(k_tg.volt, float(Vtgs[0]))
interruptible_sleep(10)

# Row layout: time,B,TG,BG,T_sample,I_TG,I_BG,sr0_X,sr0_P,sr1_X,sr1_P.
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
for _channel in (T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P):
    s.plot('time', _channel)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X)

_leak = {'consecutive': 0}
def fan_leak_guard(station, data):
    itg, ibg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    _leak['consecutive'] = _leak['consecutive'] + 1 if max(itg, ibg) > 1e-9 else 0
    if _leak['consecutive'] >= 2:
        print(f'LEAK TRIP: B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, TG={float(data[2]):+.4f} V, '
              f'|I_TG|={itg:.3e} A, |I_BG|={ibg:.3e} A')
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(fan_leak_guard, ())

_fan_result = s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs],
                               slow_delay=0, fast_delay=2.4)
if _fan_result.metadata.get('interrupted'):
    print(f'interrupted: actual B={magnet.field():+.4f} T, TG={k_tg.volt():+.4f} V, BG={k_bg.volt():+.4f} V')
    raise RuntimeError('Fan interrupted; inspect partial data and actual state before another move')
# Park the gates only after a completed/clean sweep; keep B at 10 T for next arc step.
s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0.0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0.0)
print(f'done: B={magnet.field():+.3f} T, TG={k_tg.volt():+.4f} V, BG={k_bg.volt():+.4f} V')
